title: Access control is the finding that shows up in most SOC 2 reports
angle: The most common SOC 2 exceptions are not exotic. They are access reviews that were written down and then not done, which is a governance problem rather than a technical one.
keyPoints: Access control findings appear in the majority of SOC 2 reports, and they are largely avoidable.
Recurring specifics: terminated employees keeping access for days or weeks, shared credentials, generic admin accounts, service accounts used by several people.
A very common exception is defining a quarterly access review in policy and then not running it on schedule, not documenting that it was done, or not remediating the excess access it found.
The pattern underneath most exceptions is a control that exists in the policy document but is not followed in practice.
On evidence: export from the source system where possible, because source-system reports carry more weight than hand-edited summaries.
